requirements.text: Model a situation as a system of linear equations and solve it by matrix inversion, Cramer's rule or Gaussian elimination.

requirements.section: Applications of Matrices: Consistency of system of linear equations by rank method
requirements.text: Decide by comparing ranks whether a non-homogeneous system has a unique solution, infinitely many solutions or none, and find the solution set.
Use polynomial equations to solve geometric problems such as finding dimensions satisfying volume or area conditions.

requirements.section: Vieta's Formulae and Formation of Polynomial Equations
requirements.text: Relate the roots and coefficients of polynomial equations using Vieta's formulae, and form equations with given or transformed roots.

requirements.section: Nature of Roots and Nature of Coefficients of Polynomial Equations
requirements.text: Use the conjugate-pair theorems for imaginary and surd roots and the nature of coefficients to deduce remaining roots.

requirements.section: Nature of Roots and Nature of Coefficients of Polynomial Equations
requirements.text: Solve polynomial equations without extra information using the rational root theorem, reciprocal equations and reducible non-polynomial equations.

requirements.section: Roots of Higher Degree Polynomial Equations
requirements.text: Solve higher-degree polynomial equations using additional information such as roots in progression, partial factorisation or coefficient sums.
Apply Descartes' rule of signs to bound the numbers of positive, negative and non-real roots.
Compute the mean, variance and expectations of functions of discrete and continuous random variables and use properties of expectation.
Work with probability density functions of continuous random variables, obtaining the distribution function from the density and vice versa and computing probabilities.

requirements.section: Theoretical Distributions: Some Special Discrete Distributions
requirements.text: Define random variables on a sample space and construct the probability mass function and cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable.

requirements.section: Theoretical Distributions: Some Special Discrete Distributions
requirements.text: Recognise one-point, two-point, Bernoulli and binomial distributions and compute their probabilities, mean and variance.
requirements.why: not every part is assessed: The one-point distribution (asbern, despite its title, has only Bernoulli and two-point items) and recognising which distribution a situation follows (every item names the distribution).

requirements.text: Identify statements, form compound statements with logical connectives and construct truth tables.
Classify statement forms as tautology, contradiction or contingency, write duals, and establish logical equivalences.
Decide whether an operation is a binary operation on a set and test closure, commutativity and associativity, including operations given by tables, on matrices and modulo n.
Find identity and inverse elements for binary operations, where they exist.
Solve optimisation problems arising in geometry and real-life contexts.
Use derivatives as rates of change, solve related-rates problems, and find tangents, normals and angles between curves.
Verify the hypotheses of Rolle's theorem and Lagrange's mean value theorem and apply them to find guaranteed points or prove inequalities.
Obtain Taylor and Maclaurin series expansions of standard functions.
Evaluate indeterminate forms using l'Hopital's rule, including exponential forms.
requirements.why: not every part is assessed: The exponential indeterminate forms 0⁰ and ∞⁰ (e.g. lim x→0⁺ of xˣ); only the 1^∞ form appears (arlhop), and arlhinf's limits leave the others out.

requirements.text: Find intervals of monotonicity and local and absolute extrema using the first and second derivative tests.
Determine concavity, points of inflection, symmetry and asymptotes and use them to sketch curves.
Use linear approximation and differentials to estimate values and compute absolute, relative and percentage errors.
Identify homogeneous functions and verify or apply Euler's theorem.

requirements.section: Limit and Continuity of Functions of Two Variables
requirements.text: Evaluate limits of functions of two variables and test their continuity.
Compute first and higher-order partial derivatives and verify equality of mixed partials.

requirements.section: Linear Approximation and Differential of a Function of Several Variables
requirements.text: Find the total differential and linear approximation of a function of several variables and apply the chain rule for composite functions.

requirements.section: Definite Integral as the Limit of a Sum
requirements.text: Approximate and evaluate definite integrals as limits of Riemann sums.
requirements.why: not every part is assessed: Approximating a definite integral by a finite Riemann (left/right/mid-point) sum, and limits of sums over a general interval [a, b]; aurie only evaluates limits of sums over [0, 1].

requirements.section: Fundamental Theorems of Integral Calculus and their Applications
requirements.text: Evaluate definite integrals using the fundamental theorems and properties of definite integrals, including Bernoulli's formula.
Evaluate improper integrals and use the gamma integral.
Apply reduction formulae to evaluate integrals of powers of trigonometric functions and related forms.

requirements.section: Evaluation of Bounded Plane Area by Integration
requirements.text: Find areas bounded by curves and the axes or between two curves.

requirements.section: Volume of a Solid obtained by Revolving Area about an Axis
requirements.text: Find volumes of solids generated by revolving a region about a coordinate axis.
Determine the order and degree of a differential equation and classify it (ordinary/partial, linear/non-linear).
Form a differential equation by eliminating arbitrary constants from a family of curves.
Verify general and particular solutions and solve variables-separable equations and those reducible to it by substitution.
requirements.why: not every part is assessed: Verifying that a general solution (with arbitrary constants) satisfies a differential equation, and telling general from particular solutions: only one particular solution is verified (wr:de:bacteria-growth); the task that does this (wr:hd:verify-general) is in MATH.calculus.higher-derivatives, which is not mapped to this outcome.

requirements.section: Solution of First Order and First Degree Differential Equations
requirements.text: Solve homogeneous first-order differential equations.

requirements.section: Solution of First Order and First Degree Differential Equations
requirements.text: Solve first-order linear differential equations using an integrating factor.

requirements.section: Solution of First Order and First Degree Differential Equations
requirements.text: Set up and solve first-order models for population growth, radioactive decay, Newton's law of cooling and mixture problems.
Derive and use standard equations of parabola, ellipse and hyperbola from focus-directrix-eccentricity, finding vertices, foci, axes, latus rectum and directrices.
Find the equation of a circle from given conditions, its centre and radius from the general equation, and the position of a point relative to it.
Identify the type of conic represented by a general second-degree equation.
Write parametric equations of conics and find equations of tangents and normals to circles and conics, including the condition for y = mx + c to be a tangent.
requirements.why: not every part is assessed: Writing the parametric equations of a conic: astaneh always states the parametrisation (e.g. x = 2 cos θ, y = sin θ) in the prompt, so no item asks the learner to write it.

requirements.text: Model real-life situations such as arches, reflectors, orbits and cables with conics and solve for required measurements.
Write vector and Cartesian equations of lines in space; find the angle between lines, their point of intersection and the shortest distance between skew or parallel lines.
Use dot and cross products to prove geometric and trigonometric results and to compute work done and torque.
Compute scalar and vector triple products, interpret them as volume and coplanarity tests, and apply Lagrange's and Jacobi's identities.

requirements.section: Different forms of Equation of a Straight line
requirements.text: Write equations of planes in normal, intercept and point forms, through three points or containing given lines, and find angles and distances involving planes.

requirements.section: Meeting point of a line and a plane
requirements.text: Find the image of a point in a plane and the point where a line meets a plane.

requirements.section: Sine Function and Inverse Sine Function
requirements.text: Use domain, range, period and amplitude to describe graphs of trigonometric functions and explain why restrictions are needed for inverses.

requirements.section: Sine Function and Inverse Sine Function
requirements.text: State domains and ranges of the six inverse trigonometric functions and sketch their graphs.
requirements.why: not every part is assessed: Sketching the graphs of cot⁻¹, sec⁻¹ and cosec⁻¹; the written tasks sketch only cos⁻¹, sin⁻¹ and tan⁻¹.

requirements.section: Principal Value of Inverse Trigonometric Functions
requirements.text: Find principal values of inverse trigonometric expressions.
Apply properties of inverse trigonometric functions, such as sum formulae and composition rules, to simplify expressions, prove results and solve equations.

priorities.name: Combine functions by sum, difference, product, quotient and composition
Perform and describe reflections, translations and rotations of figures
Sum special series of natural numbers
Apply the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem and its converse
